status_summary: No order, rule or FDA policy imposing a longer post-employment cooling-off period for FDA reviewers or other regulators was found since 2025-01-20. On 2025-04-17 FDA announced a policy limiting employees of regulated companies from serving as members of its advisory committees, a parallel step that keeps industry employees out of one advisory role but does not address regulators leaving for industry. Separately, Executive Order 14148 of 2025-01-20 revoked Executive Order 13989, the 2021 ethics pledge order that had set post-employment and revolving-door restrictions for political appointees, and a Federal Register search found no replacement pledge order.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14148 (signed 2025-01-20, published 2025-01-28) revoked Executive Order 13989, Ethics Commitments by Executive Branch Personnel.

FDA announced a policy limiting employees of FDA-regulated companies from serving as members of FDA advisory committees where statute permits, with rare exceptions; they may still attend and present as members of the public or serve as statutory representative members.

title: Long cooling-off periods for FDA reviewers; limit industry executives joining regulators

The FDA advisory committee policy was read on the FDA press release in review. The CRS report cited gives background on ethics pledges. No bill on cooling-off periods was checked; none is cited by this record.
